From: Ben Park <ben.park@seoulpantry.example>
To: Miguel Vance <miguel.vance@coastlinecold.example>
Date: Fri, 23 Oct 2026 10:00:00 +0000
Subject: [FROZEN LTL] TEST-C8 / PO# SYNC8PO1 / SO# SYNC8SO1 / COMMERCE,CA - SCHAUMBURG,IL 60173

Dear Miguel,

Please send quote for below.

PO# SYNC8PO1
Commodity: Frozen Vegetable Dumplings / Frozen Rice Cakes
2 Pallet ~ 3,980 lbs
REFER (FROZEN)

Pick up: ColdVault
Requested pick up date: 10/28/26 or 10/29/26

Deliver to: 300 E. Lake Dr., Schaumburg, IL 60173
Delivery Date: Before or on 11/4/26

Thank you
Ben

questions.question: What's the street address for the ColdVault pickup in Commerce?
What's the consignee name at 300 E. Lake Dr., Schaumburg?
How many cases are on PO SYNC8PO1?

confirmations.statement: We'll run PO SYNC8PO1 frozen at -10°F to 0°F. Let us know if that's not right.

why: Edge case: a quote request is treated as an order-in-waiting, since a quote needs the same fields and the rate is what's being requested. The pickup is named only as a facility, so origin is filled from the order text alone (company, plus Commerce, CA from the subject line) and the street address is asked rather than pulled from the customer's profile. Of the two requested pickup dates, the earliest is kept as the ready date and pickup is left to be scheduled; 'before or on 11/4' is the delivery deadline. 'REFER (FROZEN)' with no number gets the company's standard frozen range, 0 to -10, and a flag to confirm. The TMS needs a consignee name, which the order omits, so it is asked, as is the missing case count. Updated after the TC1 review: the assumed range is also sent to the customer as a confirmation that needs no reply.
